We must pray therefore that he whose help we turn away from us by sinning would deign, by his goodness, to make his face shine upon us, that, rescuing us from our enemies, he may grant everlasting peace.
06_marg150: It is the priests' part to invoke the name of the Lord; the Lord's to accomplish what is asked. Let no one therefore ascribe to himself what the Trinity alone grants to whom it will.
06_marg151: Allegorically. The Church, or the perfect, in whom the spices of virtues and prayers are burnt; or the humanity of Christ, in which he presented to the Father the victim of our redemption. For he himself is priest, himself victim and altar, because, holding death in his power, he took it up of his own will. Whence: No man taketh my life away from me, but I lay it down, and I take it up again.
06_interl181: the elect ordained to diverse ministries
06_marg152: THE PRINCES OF ISRAEL etc. The patriarchs, prophets and apostles, who by doctrine, example and good working offered gifts pleasing to God, and contributed with glad mind whatever good they could to the building of the Church. Tropologically too they can be called princes who, instructed in the apostolic doctrine, rightly rule the senses of the body as well as the affections of the mind; whose gifts are most pleasing to God because brought with one accord. Whence: If two of you shall consent upon earth concerning any thing whatsoever they shall ask, it shall be done to them by my Father.
06_interl183: of the various orders or churches
06_interl184: covered with boards, that they may receive the loads within, or spread with cloths, that they may more worthily receive the furniture of the tabernacle
06_marg153: The wagons which the children of Israel offered to the Levites for carrying the tabernacle signify the temporal comforts which devout peoples render to preachers, that without care or hindrance they may be free for the divine service, and that they who preach the Gospel may live by the Gospel. For if they sow spiritual things, it is no great matter if they reap temporal things.
06_marg154: Covered wagons, adorned with faith and the affection of mercy, that they may be acceptable to God. There are twelve oxen. For those who labour in the service of the saints do all things honourably and in order under the yoke of the apostolic doctrine. Or by the oxen we take the teachers who work worthily in the Lord's field, of whom it is said: "Thou shalt not muzzle the mouth of the ox that treadeth out the corn." For those who keep the apostolic rule by living and preaching are to be counted worthy of double honour.
06_interl185: because one office of charity is accepted, ministered as well by mind as by body: "For God loveth a cheerful giver."
06_marg155: Because unity of faith and simplicity of intention with devout labour please most in teachers. Nor should it be passed over that twelve embraces each man, and the fulness of time, and the site of the world. For man consists of three qualities in the soul and four in the body; and if you multiply three by four, or the reverse, twelve will come out. The world too is bounded by twelve winds, the year by twelve months, and the day by twelve hours. From all these we gather that every man, in every place, at every time, ought to hasten to the tabernacle of God with due service.
06_marg156: It is written above that the sons of Caath must carry on their own shoulders the tabernacle of the covenant, the holy of holies, the ark, the altar, the table, the candlestick and all their vessels wrapped in cloths; that the office of the Gersonites is to carry the curtains of the tabernacle, and the roof and the other covering, and over all the violet covering, and the hanging that hangs in the entry of the tabernacle, the curtains of the court, and all that pertains to the brazen altar, the cords and the vessels of the ministry; and of the Merarites, to carry the boards of the tabernacle, its bars, pillars and their vessels, and the pillars of the court round about with their sockets, pins and cords. Note therefore that the things which are holy are not laid on dumb animals to be carried, but on rational ones. The harder and heavier things, then, are laid on dumb animals, and among these there is a difference. For those who keep the harder and heavier ministries have more animals. For four wagons are given to the sons of Merari; but for the sons of Gerson, who are nearest to the sons of Caath, two suffice. Whence it is shown that more serve the harder and coarser works, as it were like animals. But to the things which are seen to by rational men, few of the less learned come. The mystical secrets lie open to the priests alone; no animal man comes near, nor even those who seem to have some exercise and learning.
06_marg157: Each one ought to offer according to his power faith, doctrine and good working for the progress and honour of the Church.
06_marg158: In the time of the incarnation, when after the resurrection and ascension the disciples received the outpouring of the Holy Ghost.
06_marg159: The preachers, leaders on the right way, who, though they offer the same doctrine of faith and the same examples of good work, yet distribute their offerings according to the diversity of place and time.
06_interl187: a vessel in which vinegar is put
06_marg160: A DISH etc. These have a narrow mouth, and signify the narrowness of the letter of the law and the obscurity of the prophets.
06_marg161: The various vessels made for offering libations are the various distinctions of the word according to the various capacity of the hearers. For the wise are to be taught one way, the foolish another, the rich one way, the poor another, the healthy one way, the sick another; the rude people of the Jews one way under the shadow of the law, the Christian another in the truth of the Gospel.
06_marg162: The spiritual knowledge is in the law and in the Gospel, which was written and put forth for the salvation of men by the ministry of spiritual grace; hence the sacrifice is rightly made, because nothing is so acceptable to God as meditation on the law with the carrying out of work.
06_marg163: The bowl was formerly made of glass: for hyalim is Greek, vitrum Latin; and, being broad at the top, it signifies the light of the Gospel, by which all the mysteries of the law and the prophets are explained; also the apostolic doctrine, by which all the riddles of the law became clear. And well are the dishes of one hundred and thirty sicles of silver, because of the Decalogue of the law and the age of the lawgiver, which was one hundred and twenty years. The bowls too are of seventy sicles, where the number ten multiplied seven times shows that the commandments are to be fulfilled by the grace of the Holy Ghost, who was given more manifestly in the New Testament.
06_marg164: The heart of the elect, full of divine wisdom, containing the spices of the virtues. Whence it is said: For the multitude of believers had but one heart and one soul.
06_marg165: Because with the fulfilling of the ten commandments they send forth the odour of doctrine and prayer, that they may merit to receive the penny of eternal life.
06_marg166: AN OX OF THE HERD etc. These signify the diverse persons of the Fathers who went before, who are examples to us. For some performed the offices of teacher, others were set over subjects in leadership and kingship, others were either most holy or most pleasing by the simplicity and meekness of their conversation, others most acceptable by penance done bravely and worthily.
06_marg167: Tropologically. He offers an ox who spends useful labour on his neighbours in the Church of God; a ram, who directs himself and others in the way of justice; a lamb of a year old, who is simple and innocent. All these for a holocaust, for the love of God alone and the desire of eternal life. He offers a buck goat for sin who does not cease to repent and pray for his sins. For a sacrifice of peace offerings he offers two oxen who with good works fulfils the two precepts of charity, namely love of God, by keeping his commandments, and of neighbour, by providing for his needs; on which dependeth the whole law and the prophets. And he offers five rams, five buck goats, five lambs of a year old, who leads the five senses of the body bravely in the way of truth, restrains them from sins, and sets forth examples of simplicity.
06_marg168: TWO THOUSAND FOUR HUNDRED. Allegorically. In the silver vessels, which all together have two thousand four hundred sicles by the weight of the sanctuary, we take the perfect doctrine of the word of God, which consists in the two Testaments; to which, if we rightly obey, the four-horse chariot of the virtues, that is, prudence, justice, fortitude and temperance, will bring us to eternal beatitude. For the thousand doubled shows that the two Testaments show us the way to beatitude; and the four hundred, that with the perfection of good works we come there in the chariot of the virtues: for unless one runs by good acts, one does not come there.
06_marg169: Allegorically. The twelve golden little mortars, each of which has ten sicles, and all together one hundred and twenty sicles of gold, signify that the hearts of the elect keep the knowledge of the law in all things according to the apostolic doctrine. For twelve tens make one hundred and twenty, the number with which the first Church in Jerusalem received the Spirit the Paraclete. Whence is added: By the weight of the sanctuary. For the sanctuary is the Church, following whose rule of faith and understanding we believe that all things written in the law and the prophets are wholesome for us. But whatever is thought and understood or kept outside the unity of the Church brings forth the damnation of the soul.
06_marg170: The oxen, rams and lambs, comprised in the number twelve, signify those who, either in the office of teacher, or in the rule of some honour, or living simply, strive to do all things according to the apostolic and prophetic doctrine.
06_marg171: These are they who strive to perform penance according to the rule of the apostolic faith.
06_marg172: In these is signified spiritual knowledge with the perfection of good works, because twenty-four, the number of hours in which the course of a day is run, signifies that the light of knowledge and faith is necessary to every Christian.
06_marg173: Sixty, that is, six times ten, shows the perfection of the commandments. For it is necessary that prelates, subjects and penitents do all things according to the doctrine of the Church, so that their oblation may keep the rite and order of peace offerings, and they may merit the grace of God, not his offence.
06_interl191: the preachers, the teachers of the people
06_interl192: namely, by meditating on holy Scripture, whence God speaks
06_marg174: GREGORY. What is it that Moses so often goes in and out, except that he who within is rapt into contemplation is pressed outside by the affairs of the weak? Within he considers the secrets of God, outside he carries the burdens of the carnal. He who on doubtful matters always runs back to the tabernacle consults the Lord before the ark of the testimony, giving an example to teachers, that when outside they are in doubt what to order, they should always return to the mind as to the tabernacle, and consult God as before the ark of the testimony; and in the things about which they are in doubt within themselves, they should search the pages of the sacred word within. Whence: Christ clings to prayer on the mountain, works miracles in the cities; laying down for good rulers the way of imitation, that if they already seek the highest things by contemplating, they should yet be mingled with the needs of the weak by compassion. For charity rises wonderfully to the heights when it draws itself mercifully to the low things of neighbours; and the more kindly it comes down to the lowest, the more strongly it runs back to the highest.
06_marg175: Because through the grace of divine propitiation, after the fault of transgression, God opened to us the way of truth.
06_marg176: Because God did not appear to Moses in his own substance, but through an angelic vision. Whence: The law ordained by angels in the hand of a mediator. Or because through both Testaments he instructs us with a harmonious voice to the faith of truth. Or because through the Son, who appeared in the flesh in the midst of the two Testaments, the Father spoke to the human race.
06_marg177: The seven gifts of the Holy Ghost, which always remained in Christ and are distributed in the members according to his will.
06_interl193: the sacred Scripture of the Gospel
06_marg178: The table and the candlestick: the temporal benefits of God by which we are refreshed and enlightened, so that, strengthened by these, as the grace of merits grows, we may come to eat the bread of angels in heaven and to see the true light of God. These are without the veil, because only in this life do we need Scriptures and teachers and the other sacraments; but in the future the Lord will show us plainly of the Father. The south side of the tabernacle signifies the ancient people of God, which first received the light of divine knowledge and the fervour of love; the north, the Church gathered from the Gentiles, which remained longer in darkness. Rightly therefore the candlestick, which is on the south side, signifies the grace given to the former people; and the table on the north side, the benefits of God given to us. Well therefore is the candlestick set over against the table, because the Scripture of the law and the prophets looks toward the grace of the Gospel, bearing witness to it.
06_marg179: UPON THE CANDLESTICK: namely, upon Christ, the firstborn from the root of Jesse, "upon" whom rested "the spirit of wisdom and of understanding, the spirit of counsel and of fortitude" etc.
06_marg180: Because Christ is singularly free from sin and renowned for works of justice; and the members, who imitate his innocence as they are able, will be perfected in the future.
06_marg181: Because Christ from his conception and birth was perfect God and man, bore the pains of the passions, and so came to the glory of the resurrection; and all who will to live godly in him, as metal widened by beating, come through the insults of the passion to the grace of immortality.
06_marg182: Christ, namely, from whom the branches proceed, because from him the just receive whatever good they have. Whence: "Without me you can do nothing."
06_marg183: Mystically. He instructs the ecclesiastical order how it is duly to be advanced to the dignity of the priesthood.
06_interl194: namely of baptism, or of tears, by which the stains of sins are washed away
06_interl195: not: pluck out; because the roots remain, from which they may grow again.
06_interl196: the thoughts of the old life
06_marg184: GREGORY. The hairs of the flesh are any superfluous thoughts of human flesh or of the old life, which we so cut from the mind that we are wearied by no grief at their loss. And Levite is said to mean taken up. The Levites therefore must shave all the hairs of the flesh, because he who is taken up into the service of God ought to appear before the eyes of God clean of all thoughts of the flesh, lest the mind put forth unlawful thoughts and make the beautiful appearance of the soul unsightly as with darkening hairs. But however high the virtue of holy conversation has raised anyone, there still grows in him from the oldness of life something to remove. Whence the hairs of the Levites themselves are commanded to be shaved, not plucked out. For when the hairs are shaved, the roots remain in the flesh and grow, that they may be cut again. Because superfluous thoughts must be cut off with great zeal, but they cannot be cut off utterly. For superfluous things are always being produced, which the spirit cuts back with the steel of carefulness. But we do this more finely in ourselves when we penetrate the heights of contemplation.
06_marg185: They have cleansed, namely, their works, that their conversation may be clean in the sight of God and blameless before men.
06_marg186: The Mediator of God and men, by whose immolation our sins are blotted out. In both oxen his incarnation is signified. For the passion of Christ is one, but it obtained two things for us, namely expiation from sins and sanctification, that he might offer us to God sanctified in the flesh and quickened in the spirit. Whence Paul: But you are washed, but you are sanctified in the name of the Lord Jesus. By these two oxen, of which one is offered for sin and the other for a holocaust, two kinds of actions can be expressed: by one we wash away by the lament of penance the evil we have done; by the other we merit the grace of God and the reward of beatitude by the fruits of good works and virtues.
06_interl198: begotten of the patriarchs and prophets
06_marg187: The sacrament of the passion, which, understood and handled with spiritual knowledge, is most wholesome to the faithful and most pleasing to God; if only the minister of God shows himself clean and worthy within and without for receiving such mysteries.
06_marg188: The Levites are brought before the tabernacle of the covenant when those chosen for the office of the altar are brought forward according to the apostolic doctrine, by which the true tabernacle is entered; if, namely, they have begun well according to the doctrine and examples of the saints, and have persevered to the end.
06_marg189: THEY SHALL PUT. Because they ought to give assent to the choice of their devotion, and at their command to press on in good works.
06_interl199: the true one of the mountain, that is, Christ
06_marg190: The choice, namely, is to be made under the testimony and knowledge of many, that a worthy examination may be held, so that no one can find fault. For they ought to have a good testimony even from them that are without.
06_marg191: THE LEVITES ALSO etc. Because the ministers of the Lord hasten to consecrate to the Lord by their own labour the beginnings of good works, that, whether penance is to be done or the pursuits of virtues exercised, they may carry them out effectually.
06_marg192: The minister of the Lord ought not to be content with the discipline of the common people. He ought to be set apart and conspicuous in manners and doctrine.
06_marg193: Allegorically. ORIGEN. The firstborn of the Egyptians are the beginnings of vices, by which human life is corrupted. For every soul, when it has come to the fulness of age and a certain natural law, as it were, has begun to defend its rights in it, produces its first motions according to the desires of the flesh, which the force of incitement stirs up by the tinder of concupiscence or anger. Whence it is said of Christ as something proper and special: "Butter and honey shall he eat", before he does or utters evil things, he shall choose the good. For before the child know good or evil, he will resist evil, that he may choose what is good. But David says of himself: "The sins of my youth and my ignorances do not remember." Because therefore the first motions of the soul, brought forth according to the flesh, rush into sin, they are rightly called the firstborn of the Egyptians, which are extinguished. But let the conversation of the rest of life direct a more amended course.
06_marg194: The vices, which are the firstborn of the devil, or the works of the flesh by which nature is defiled, being extinguished, good manners are to be put in their place. Moreover, the minister of God ought to be instructed in more perfect manners than the multitude of the people. For therefore, for the firstborn of the Egyptians, the firstborn of the Israelites are commanded to be offered to the Lord; and again, for the firstborn of the children of Israel, the Levites are taken into the service of the Lord; so that for a sinful life a just life, and for a just life a holy, proven and perfect one may be shown, that the true Levite may be worthily fitted to the altars of Christ and to the divine mysteries.
06_marg195: TO SERVE etc. Let the ministers of the Lord see how necessary it is for them to keep the rights of their office, and not to gape after earthly gains or pleasures, they whose proper part is to serve the tabernacle and pray for the people, lest there be a destroying plague among them; otherwise they cast both themselves and the people headlong into perdition, and it is said to them: "I will not receive a gift of your hand."
06_interl201: so was it done touching the Levites
06_interl202: when the wars of the vices rise up against each one
06_interl203: let them serve, namely, in the Church, not preside
06_interl204: that is: when they shall have inward rest
06_interl205: the war of the vices being laid to rest
06_marg196: FROM TWENTY-FIVE. ISIDORE. The Levites are commanded to serve the tabernacle from the twenty-fifth year, and from the fiftieth they become keepers of the vessels. By the twenty-fifth year, in which the flower of youth springs up, the wars against each of the vices are marked. By the fiftieth, the inward rest of the mind, the war being subdued, is marked. By the vessels of the tabernacle, the souls of the faithful. The Levites therefore serve the tabernacle from the twenty-fifth year, and from the fiftieth become keepers of the vessels, so that those who still endure the struggles of assailing vices through the consent of delight should not presume to take up the care of others. But when they have subdued the wars of temptations, when they are already secure within themselves of inward tranquillity, let them be allotted the keeping of souls. But who subdues these perfectly, when Paul says: I see another law in my members, fighting against the law of my mind etc.? But it is one thing to endure wars bravely, another to be overcome feebly. In the former virtue is exercised, lest it should be lifted up; in the latter it is wholly extinguished, so that it cannot stand.
06_marg197: BEDE. Let the children of Israel make the phase in its season, the fourteenth day of this month etc. Whereas in the Old Testament the paschal time is observed by three marks, namely that it be celebrated after the equinox, and in the first month, in its third week, that is, from the evening of the fourteenth moon (which is the beginning of the fifteenth) to the evening, that is, the end, of the twenty-first moon, a fourth rule has been imposed on us by the resurrection of Christ: that when, the equinox passed, we have seen the moon of the first month rise in the evening on the fourteenth, we do not at once make the pasch, but, waiting for the Lord's day, on which he himself celebrated the pasch, that is, the passage from death to life, by rising, we celebrate the pasch on it. And if anyone objects that the Lawgiver set down no mention of the equinox, but only of the first month and the third week, let him know that, although he does not name the equinox expressly, yet in commanding the pasch to be made from the full moon of the first month he declares the passing of the equinox. Since it is agreed that the moon which first shows its full orb after the equinox has passed is the moon of the first month. As often, therefore, as we have the Lord's day as soon as the fifteenth moon comes, our paschal time differs in nothing from the legal one, although we keep the pasch with other kinds of sacraments. And as often as the same Lord's day falls on the second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth or seventh day from then, not even then do we destroy the law and the prophets. For as the observance of so many paschal ceremonies, so also the time in which it was commanded to be done, breathes of sacred mysteries. For first we take care, according to the decree of the law, that the equinox be passed, so that the solemnity (in which Christ, the power of darkness destroyed, opened to the world the way of light) may by the very order of time show outwardly what it holds within; and that the feast which promises us the light of eternal beatitude may be celebrated chiefly then, when the sun, advancing by its yearly increase, takes its first victory over the shadow of night. Then we attend to the first month of the year, which is also called the month of new things, in which to celebrate the pasch; that is, the month in which this world was formed and the first man set in the seat of paradise; because through this solemnity we hope to receive again the first robe and the first kingdom from which we departed into a far country. Whence Peter: But we look for new heavens and a new earth according to his promises. And elsewhere: "Behold, I make all things new."
06_marg198: Then we observe the third week, which accords with the Lord's resurrection, which took place on the third day, and in the third age of the world, that is, when with the coming of heavenly grace his whole dispensation in the flesh appeared to the world, consummated by the glory of the resurrection. For he enlightened the first times of the world by the natural law through the fathers, the middle by the written law or the prophets, the last by the spiritual gift through himself.
06_marg199: The very turning of the moon also signifies to us a heavenly sacrament. For the moon, being of round shape, receives light from the sun. Therefore it is always bright on the half of its orb which it has toward the sun, but always dark on the other half. From the first to the fifteenth it has increase of light toward the earth, but lack toward the heavens; from the fifteenth to the last, the reverse. This turning of it rightly signifies the mysteries of the paschal joy, by which we are taught to turn all the glory of our mind away from earthly things and hang it on the light of heavenly grace alone. Or the light of the moon, growing to human eyes, hints at the grace of the virtues with which the Lord, appearing in the flesh, shone upon the world; of which it is said: And Jesus advanced in age and wisdom and grace with God and men. But turning back toward the heavens, it hints at the glory of the resurrection and ascension, which in itself came at once to perfection, but in the mind of the faithful grows by certain advances of its light until the end of the world. For the Lord, rising, appeared first to individuals, then to two, then to more, now to seven, now to eleven, now to twelve, now to more than five hundred brethren together, and last to all the disciples; and, about to ascend into heaven in their sight, he commanded them to be "witnesses" of his dispensation "even to the uttermost part of the earth".
06_marg200: And well does the moon, when it grows to our eyes, gradually withdraw from the sun, but when toward the heavens, return to it by equal spaces. For this is what he says: "I came forth from the Father, and am come into the world", and "again I leave the world, and I go to the Father." And David says: "His going out is from the end of heaven, and his circuit even to the end thereof." Because therefore the moon, by the increase of light which, going out from the sun, it turns to our gaze, signifies Christ's doctrine and virtues in the flesh up to the passion; and by gathering back its light, returning to the sun, gradually to the face of heaven invisible to us, shows the miracles of the resurrection and the later glory, the fifteenth is rightly fitted to the paschal joy.
06_marg201: To these marks of the Pasch or Phase taken from the law, we heirs of the New Testament also join the Lord's day, because it excels both by the creation of the first light and by the triumph of the Lord's resurrection.
06_marg202: The seven days of the moon also, that is, from the fifteenth day to the twenty-first, through which that Lord's day runs in natural order, signify the whole Church throughout the world redeemed by the paschal mysteries. For seven signifies universality. Whence: "Seven times a day I have given praise to thee." That is: "His praise shall be always in my mouth." Whence John too, writing to the seven churches of Asia, shows the mysteries of the universal Church; whence, writing exhortations to each, he watchfully repeats: He that hath ears to hear, let him hear what the Spirit saith to the churches; as if: What I say to one, I say to all.
06_marg203: In the name too of Pasch or Phase we are morally admonished to pass over from vices to virtues. In the month of new things (in which the grown fruits, by their coming, announce the ceasing of the old), that we put off the old man with his deeds and put on the new, and, quickened by the variety of diverse virtues and veiled by their leaves as by the shade of a pleasant tree, spring up as glad and fruitful crops. At the full moon, that, bearing the perfect splendour of faith and understanding, we may be separated from the darkness of sin. In the light turned back toward the heavens, which begins from the fifteenth moon, that the greater we are, the more we may humble ourselves in all things, saying: By the grace of God I am what I am. And because this grace of the heavenly gift was poured forth more manifestly in the third age of the world, by a most beautiful sequence of the figure, in the third week of the moon its light, which until then had grown toward the earth, begins to grow toward heavenly things. Beautifully we are commanded to observe this week at the Pasch, that, mindful of the grace received, we may through each step of the spiritual passage repay the giver of it.
06_marg204: Or in the moon growing toward men the active life is shown, in the one turned back toward the heavens the contemplative. Or in this turning, love of neighbour; in that, of God. Or the advance of light turned hither admonishes us to do good works outwardly; turned thither, to do the same works with regard only to the heavenly reward. Hither, that "your light may shine before men, that they may see your good works"; thither, "that they may glorify your Father who is in heaven". On the first day of the week, which is the proper solemnity of the New Testament, we are instructed to bear all things for Christ, and death itself, patiently, in the hope of our future resurrection in Christ. Because if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead dwell in us, he shall quicken also our mortal bodies. And whose Spirit (because his grace is sevenfold) can fittingly be understood by the same number of seven lunar days through which the Lord's day, the first of the week, is carried round.
06_interl209: on account of the touching of some dead body
06_marg205: BUT BEHOLD SOME WHO WERE UNCLEAN BY OCCASION OF THE SOUL OF A MAN etc. AUGUSTINE. When at the time of the Pasch some were unclean by occasion of the soul of a man, and asked how they should make the Pasch, since they had to be purified from uncleanness for seven days according to the law, Moses consults the Lord. And he received the answer that whoever this had befallen, or who, being far off, could not come, should make the Pasch in another month, because of the fourteenth day of the month, where the number of the moon was observed. But if it is asked what they would do if perhaps such uncleanness befell them even at the second month, I think that what was said of the second month was to be held as a rule, so that they would observe it in the third month. Or perhaps, if they had not kept the Pasch, it would not count as a fault.
06_marg206: GREGORY. Moses often runs back to the tabernacle on doubtful matters, leaving the crowds. To return to the tabernacle is to enter the secret place of the mind, the tumults of outward things being set aside. For there the Lord is consulted, and what is to be done publicly outside is heard silently within. Good rulers also do this daily, when they know they cannot discern doubtful matters, and, returning to the secret place of the mind as to a kind of tabernacle, having looked into the divine law, consult the Lord as if before the ark set there. And what they first hear within in silence they afterward make known outside in action. For that they may serve outward things without offence, they take care to run back unceasingly to the secret places of the heart, and so hear the voice of the Lord as by a hidden inspiration, while in the meditation of the mind they are drawn away from the carnal senses.
06_interl210: the Gentile, defiled in soul with all vices, and having committed fornication with demons
06_interl211: from God, because without the faith of one God, without the Law
06_marg207: ISIDORE. It is commanded that those who dwelt farther off, or had been unclean in soul, should make the Pasch in the second month, because the Gentiles, having committed fornication with all the demons, were unclean and far from God. But, cleansed by wholesome confession, they are commanded to pass over to the nativity of Christ as to the second month.
06_marg208: RABANUS. He is unclean in soul who is defiled by diabolical deceit through the worship of idols and the enormity of sins. He is on a journey far off who, hearing the word of salvation, chooses to forsake idols and receive the faith, but has not yet come to baptism, by which one enters the Church, that is, Jerusalem, the city of peace, where are the house and the holy of holies. For the flesh of the lamb is commanded to be eaten in one house, because outside the Church it is not lawful to eat the body of Christ. The Gentile people therefore (because it could not keep the first Pasch according to the law), in the second month, that is, in the time of grace, now cleansed from all uncleanness of sins and restored to the house, where it is lawful to make the Phase, eats the lamb at the evening of the world with unleavened bread and wild lettuce.
06_marg209: He eats unleavened bread who does right works without the corruption of vainglory, and the commandments of mercy without admixture of sin.
06_marg210: Because when we receive the body of Christ we ought to be pricked with compunction for sins, that the bitterness of penance may wipe away the love of a perverse life.
06_marg211: Whatever was commanded historically in the law in the celebration of the Pasch, the Church observes spiritually.
06_marg212: Because his sayings are to be carefully examined, that they may be penetrated in the present life by understanding and working.
06_marg213: He instructs those who were under the law by threatening, lest they neglect to observe the time of the Pasch. He admonishes us also to make the spiritual Pasch in its time, of which Paul says: "Behold, now is the acceptable time" etc. Because whoever has not celebrated with worthy faith the redemption of the human race, which was made by the immolation of the true lamb, and has not turned his life to better things, and has not passed over from vices to virtues in the time of this mortality, will have no part in the glory of the resurrection to be given at the end to the true worshippers of Christ, but will be cut off from the fellowship of the saints.
06_marg214: He shows that there is no respect of persons with God. For whoever, converted to the catholic faith and washed with the baptism of Christ, has entered the unity of the Church can share in the ecclesiastical mysteries.
06_marg215: ISIDORE. Christ is the pillar, who is upright and firm and props up our weakness, shining by night, not shining by day, that they who see not may see, and they who see may become blind. The sacrament of Christ too is manifest as in the day, in the flesh, as in a cloud; but in the judgment as in the terror of the night. Because then there will be great tribulation, like fire, and it will give light to the just and burn the unjust.
06_marg216: The incarnation of Christ, whose clemency protects the tabernacle of the Church, whose goodness orders its state, whose prudence directs its passage on the way of this world.
06_marg217: In the fire, terror; in the cloud, the gentle charm of vision. The day is the life of the just, the night that of the sinner. Whence: You were heretofore darkness, but now light in the Lord. In the day therefore the pillar is shown by a cloud, in the night by fire, because God will appear gentle to the just, terrible to the unjust. These, coming in the judgment, he will soothe with the mildness of gentleness; those he will terrify with the justice of strictness. The pillar of cloud went before the people in the desert, shining with the splendour of fire not in the day but in the night, because Christ, by the example of his conversation, giving leadership to those who follow, shone with no light to those who trust in their own justice, but shone with the fire of his love on those who acknowledge the darkness of their sins.
06_interl214: at the sign, namely, of the cloud for standing or moving, by which God commanded them either to stand or to move
06_interl215: keeping, namely, the precept of the Lord
06_interl216: others: But if for two days or a month
06_marg218: The signification of the cloud, which was the sign of the divine will, like the voice of one speaking.
06_marg219: MAKE THEE TWO TRUMPETS etc. ISIDORE. And a little after: When a broken sound shall ring out, the camps shall move etc. By two trumpets the army is led, because by the two Testaments or the two precepts of charity the people is called out to the readiness of faith. These are commanded to be made of silver, that the words of preachers may shine with the brightness of eloquence and confound the mind of the hearers by no obscurity of their own. And they are beaten, because those who preach the life to come must grow through the blows of present tribulations. And well is it said: When a broken sound shall ring out, the camps shall move. Because when a finer and more detailed preaching is handled, the minds of the hearers are roused more ardently to the struggles of temptations.
06_marg220: RABANUS. To sound the trumpets once is to put forth the word of doctrine according to the unity of faith and the concord of the catholic sense. At this sound the princes and the heads of the multitude ought to come together, so that those who preside over the rest, united in faith and love, may faithfully confer about their own salvation and that of their people, and show an example of peace and concord; lest there be among them "envying and contention", but that "all speak the same thing in the same mind and in the same judgment".
06_marg221: To whom, namely, the light of faith first shone. When, therefore, the preachers of the Gospel were ordained, it is said to them first: Go ye not into the way of the Gentiles, but go ye rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel; to whom Christ himself preached the Gospel in person. But after the resurrection, appearing to the disciples, he says: Going therefore teach ye all nations etc. The tribe of Juda therefore, with the others who dwelt with it on the east, first moved camp; then the others according to their order. Because the first Church had first to be built in Judea, and afterward the nations from all the peoples of the world called to the faith.
06_marg222: RABANUS. In the calling together of the people, the sound of the trumpets is commanded to be plain and not broken, because he who preaches the word of faith to a multitude ought to speak simply and openly, so that many may understand and be edified; lest, if he preaches obscurely and strangely, the hearers go away empty. Whence Paul: Brethren, if I come to you speaking with tongues, what shall I profit you, unless I speak to you either in revelation, or in knowledge, or in prophecy, or in doctrine? etc. And a little after: "Let all things be done to edification." For a word too obscure or ambiguous ought to be said in the manner of the common people, so that it may be understood even by the unlearned. For what does correctness of speech profit, if it does not edify the hearers? For we speak to no purpose if we are not understood by those for whose sake we speak. He therefore who teaches should avoid all words that do not teach; and if instead of them he can say correct words that are understood, let him rather choose those. But if there are none, or they do not occur at the moment, let him use less correct words, provided the matters are correctly taught and learned. And not only in private conversations, but still more when the people is called together. And the best manner of learning is that by which it comes about that he who hears hears the truth and understands it; and it is the mark of a good disposition to love the truth in words, not the words. For what does a golden key profit if it does not open? For we seek nothing but that what is shut may lie open.
06_marg223: The preachers, namely, preach the word of God and show the way of justice to the hearers, that they may set the step of good work in the path of God's commandments and flee the road of the wicked.
06_interl217: because it is proper to priests to preach the Gospel
06_interl218: the care of earthly things, namely, being cast away
06_marg224: By rousing, namely, those subject to them to penance and to the compunction of tears, and by provoking the hearts of the hearers to implore the mercy of God.
06_marg225: RABANUS. Note that he commanded the trumpets to be sounded in adversity and in prosperity, because every time is fitting for the word of God. For now it is to be read, now to be sung to God; now it is fitting to pray, now to teach, now to exhort, now to rebuke; because the speech of teachers is to be tempered according to the quality of the hearers. Whence: "I will bless the Lord at all times, his praise shall be always in my mouth." And elsewhere: "Preach the word, be instant in season, out of season" etc.
06_marg226: JEROME. At the twelfth station the children of Israel came into the desert of Sinai, on the forty-seventh day from their going out of Egypt. Whence in Exodus: In the third month of the departure of the children of Israel out of Egypt, on this day they came into the wilderness of Sinai. For departing out of Raphidim, they came into the desert of Sinai, and they camped in the wilderness, and Moses went up to God. And the Lord called unto him from the mountain etc. And again: Go, he says, to the people, and sanctify them today and tomorrow, and let them wash their garments, and let them be ready against the third day etc. Let us reckon the number, and we shall find that the law was given on mount Sinai on the fiftieth day of the departure; whence also the solemnity of Pentecost is celebrated, and the sacrament of the Gospel is completed by the descent of the Holy Ghost. At this station are described the middle part of Exodus, the whole of Leviticus, and no small precepts of Numbers, and the distribution of the people by each tribe, and the offering of the princes. And Sinai is interpreted "of the bramble", not one, as above in the wilderness of Sin, but many; so that there is the beginning, here the perfection; there a single number, here a manifold. For it is one thing to possess one grace, another to possess all. Israel therefore, after the familiar speech with the Lord, having stayed by mount Sinai one year and four days, went out with a wonderful ordering of the camps into the wilderness of Pharan, which is interpreted "wild ass" or "wildness"; and there it gave way to the evil beast, loathing the heavenly bread and desiring the flesh of the Egyptians, when a sudden fire devoured many, and at the intercession of Moses the devouring flame was swallowed up by the ground. Then they receive quails and devour them to nausea. Seventy elders are chosen, and go to the door of the tabernacle; two remain, Eldad and Medad, not neglectful of the command, but bowed down by humility, judging themselves unworthy of the honour; whence also, though absent, they prophesy. And when the people was filled, while the meat was yet in their mouth, "the wrath of God came upon them, and he slew the fat ones amongst them, and brought down the chosen men of Israel", that they might not run swiftly to evil. Whence the place was called "the graves of lust", or according to the Septuagint, "of the memory of desire". From these we are taught, we who leave worldly knowledge and have despised the Egyptian fleshpots, that we ought not to murmur against the heavenly bread of Scripture, nor seek the poisons of the Egyptians, who are of great flesh, but the simple food of manna. But if we wish to seek them again, we shall devour to nausea, and at once be tormented by the fire of the Lord, and our desire will be turned into tombs, so that we are whited sepulchres, which outwardly appear to men beautiful, but within are full of dead men's bones and of all filthiness.
06_marg227: GREGORY. Often we can better persuade the proud to useful things if we say that their progress will profit us rather than them, if we ask that their bettering be bestowed on us rather than on them. For the pride of such a one is easily bent to good if his bending is believed to profit others. Whence Moses, who was going on with God ruling him and the pillar leading, when he wished to lead his kinsman out of the conversation of the Gentiles and bring him under the dominion of God, said: We are going towards the place which the Lord will give us etc. And when he had answered: I will not go with thee etc., he at once added: Do not leave us: for thou knowest in what places we should encamp in the wilderness etc. It was not ignorance of the way that straitened the mind of Moses, which the knowledge of the Godhead had opened out to the knowledge of prophecy, whom the pillar and the divine converse instructed. But the provident man, speaking to a proud hearer, asked for comfort that he might give it; he sought a guide on the way for one whose guide he might become to life. He so acted, then, that the proud hearer might be the more devoted to the voice persuading him to better things, the more he was thought necessary; and from the very place where he believed he was going before his exhorter, he might bow to the words of the one exhorting.
06_interl228: by the faith of the Trinity, showing the way of truth in three times
06_marg228: RABANUS. The ark of the covenant of the Lord goes before the children of Israel for three days, providing places for the camps, because the incarnation of the Lord directs the journey of the present life for the elect from the beginning of the world, and truly gives leadership to the holy land; which before led the fathers of the Old Testament in figure, and now in truth shows us the way of justice. The three days' journey, therefore, is the faith of the holy Trinity. In three times, before the law, under the law, under grace, it shows the path of truth and justice to those who follow.
06_marg229: The divine protection, which by the grace of the Holy Ghost defends the elect from the beginning of the world and guards them for the rest to come.
06_marg230: By the example of Moses the rulers of the people are called on always carefully to commend the flock entrusted to them to the Lord at the beginning of the work and at its completion, that he may protect his own sheep and drive back the enemies.
06_marg231: RABANUS. The fire of the Lord, kindled, devours the murmuring people, because the fire of the Lord's great vengeance will torment in the future those who, with a tongue set on fire by hell, murmur or detract. Whence it is said by Wisdom: "The whisperer and the double-tongued is accursed." The fire devours the uttermost part of the camp, namely the end of present actions. Whence: "The Lord shall judge the ends of the earth." But he who persists uncorrected until death shall be burned with perpetual punishment both in soul and in body.
06_interl230: carnal works, to be boiled down by the labours of tribulations that are seen
06_interl232: the difficulties of the present life, which is passed not without grief, and yet is loved with tears
06_marg232: GREGORY. The minds of the carnal, for love of the world, are ready to bear certain hard things as though they were soft and delightful. While in this life they strive to lay hold of the heights of things, the Lord commands a ceasing from the labours of the world and persuades them to the sweetness of rest; and yet the mad mind of the wicked rejoices more to pursue harsh things carnally than to hold soft things spiritually. It is fed more by the bitterness of weariness than by the sweetness of rest. So the Israelites, while they received the refreshment of manna from above, desired from Egypt the fleshpots, melons, leeks and onions. For does not the manna signify grace of most sweet savour, given from above for the refreshment of the inner life to those who are well at leisure? The fleshpots, carnal works, to be boiled down by the labours of tribulations that are seen, as by fires. The melons, earthly sweetnesses. The leeks and onions, which are eaten with tears, the difficulty of the present life, which is passed not without grief and is loved with tears. Forsaking the manna, therefore, they sought leeks and onions with melons and flesh, because perverse minds despise the sweet gifts of grace given through rest, and for carnal pleasures covet the laborious journeys of this life, full even of tears. They scorn to have that wherein they may rejoice spiritually, and with longing seek that wherein they may groan carnally.
06_marg233: GREGORY. Just as those are commonly called young who are weighed down by no gravity of counsel, so Scripture calls those old, not who are ripe by length of time alone, but by gravity of manners. Whence: "Venerable old age is not that of long time, nor counted by the number of years: but the understanding of a man is grey hairs. And a spotless life is old age." Hence it is said to Moses: Gather unto me seventy men of the ancients of Israel, whom thou knowest to be ancients of the people. In which words old age of heart is noted, since such old men are commanded to be chosen as are known. For if old age of body were sought, they could be known by as many as could see them. But when it is said, whom thou knowest to be ancients of the people, it is plain that old age of mind, not of body, is chosen.
06_interl235: in the cloud of the flesh
06_interl236: the Holy one, namely, who is in thee by grace etc.
06_marg234: ISIDORE. At the thirteenth station the Spirit came down upon seventy chosen men, and the Lord came down from the cloud and took of the Spirit that was upon Moses, and put it upon the seventy men. For when Christ came down in the cloud of the flesh, the grace of the Holy Ghost was poured out through faith upon the peoples, upon the chosen out of the seventy nations, and there came upon all that gift of heavenly power which had once been in Moses and the prophets.
06_marg235: AND I WILL TAKE OF. AUGUSTINE. Another text: And I will take of the spirit which is in thee, and will put it upon them, and they shall bear with thee the onset of the people, and thou shalt not carry them alone, etc. Many Latins did not translate as it is in the Greek, but said: I will take of thy spirit which is in thee, and will put it upon them, or will put it in them; and they made the sense laborious to understand. For it may be thought to be said of the man's own spirit, by which human nature is completed when the body is joined to it, which consists of body and spirit, which they also call the soul. Whence Paul: What man knoweth the things of a man, but the spirit of a man that is in him? So the things also that are of God no man knoweth, but the Spirit of God. And what he then adds: Now we have received not the spirit of this world, but the Spirit that is of God, shows that the Spirit of God is other, of whom the spirit of man is made partaker by the grace of God. Although (as others have interpreted) the Spirit of God can also be understood when it is said, of thy spirit which is in thee, because he who is of God becomes ours also when we receive him; as it was said of John: "In the spirit and power of Elias." For the soul of Elias had not been rolled back into him. But if certain heretics think so, what do they say to that which is written: The spirit of Elias hath rested upon Eliseus, when he already had his own soul, unless that it is said of the Spirit of God, so that he worked through the one such things as he worked through Elias, not withdrawing from the one in order to fill the other, nor, being divided, less in the one so that he could be in the other? For it is God who can be as great, or whole, in all in whom he has willed to be through that grace. But now, since it is written: And I will take of the spirit which is upon thee, and it is not said, of thy spirit, it is more easily resolved; because we understand that he meant to signify nothing else than that they too would have help from the same Spirit of grace from whom Moses had it, so that these also might have as much as God willed, not so that Moses should therefore have less.
06_interl237: but he seeks the manner; he does not distrust
06_marg236: AUGUSTINE. Another text: Six hundred thousand footmen, among whom I am, and thou hast said: I will give them flesh, etc. It is asked whether Moses said this distrusting or inquiring. But if we suppose he said it distrusting, it is asked why the Lord did not reproach him for it, as he did at the rock from which the water flowed, where he seems to have doubted of the power of the Lord. But if we say he inquired the manner in which it should be done, the Lord's answer, in which it is said: Is the hand of the Lord unable?, seems to be as of one reproving him for not having believed. But I think it better understood that the Lord so answered as one who would not tell the manner he was asking, but rather show his power by the deed itself. For it could also have been objected by cavillers against Mary when she said: How shall this be done, because I know not man?, that she believed less, though she asked the manner and did not doubt of the power of God. But what was answered her: The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Most High shall overshadow thee, might also have been answered as here: Is anything impossible to the Holy Ghost, who shall come upon thee?, as if the same sense were kept. But Zachary, saying such things, is charged with unbelief and punished with the penalty of his voice stopped. For God judges not of words but of hearts; otherwise Moses could have been excused, were there not a clear sentence of God against him that he said such things distrusting: Hear, ye unbelievers. Can we bring you forth water out of this rock? And when Moses had lifted up his hand, he struck the rock twice with the rod, etc. For this he took that rod with which he had done so many miracles, and struck the rock with it, and thence obtained the effect of the accustomed power. The words therefore in which he says: Can we bring you forth water out of this rock? could be taken as though it were said: Surely out of this rock, according to your unbelief, water cannot be brought forth; so that then by striking it might be shown that what they in their unbelief did not believe could be done by God. Especially since he had said: Hear, ye unbelievers. But God, who is the inspector of the heart, showed with what mind they were said. For the Scripture says: Because you have not believed me, to sanctify me before the children of Israel, etc. And by this Moses is understood to have spoken as though he struck at uncertainty, so that if the effect did not follow, he might be thought to have foretold this when he said: Can we bring you forth water out of this rock?; which would have lain wholly hidden in his mind, had not the sentence of God betrayed it. Contrariwise, therefore, we ought to understand here that the words of Moses about the promised flesh were those of one asking how it should be done, not of one distrusting, since no sentence of God followed to punish, but rather one to teach.
06_interl238: SEPTUAGINT: Moses went out to the people and spoke the words of the Lord. For he is within while he is taught by him; when he speaks to the crowds, he is shown to go out of doors.
06_marg237: ORIGEN. Another text: Moses, it says, went out to the people, and spoke the words of the Lord. While Moses hears the words of God and is taught by him, he is within, and abides in the inner and secret places. But when he speaks to the crowds and ministers to the people, he who cannot stand within is said to go out of doors. For every teacher of the Church, if he treats of the deeper mysteries and brings forth the hidden things of wisdom among the perfect, is within. But when he speaks to the crowds the things that profit those who are without, and which the common people can hear, he goes out of doors and speaks to the people the words of God. Paul was within when he said: We speak wisdom among the perfect, etc. Going forth to the people he says: "Let no evil speech proceed from your mouth", and: "He that stole, let him now steal no more", and the like, etc.
06_marg238: It is not to be understood as though he cut a material and bodily substance into seventy portions and gave a particle to each. For it is impious to understand this of the nature of the Holy Ghost. But Moses and the Spirit that was in him were as a lamp of most bright light, from which God kindled seventy, to whom the splendour of the principal light came, and its source suffered no loss from the drawing off.
06_interl239: for purity of heart and capacity of understanding
06_marg239: ORIGEN. And the spirit rested upon them, and they all prophesied, etc. The Spirit is not read to have rested save in the saints. For he rests in those who are clean of heart, who purify their souls from sin. Just as he does not dwell in a body subject to sins, even if he once dwelt there. For he cannot suffer the fellowship of evil. And it is certain that in the time of sin an evil spirit is in the heart of each, and plays its part. When place is given it through evil thoughts and concupiscences, the Holy Ghost, saddened (so to speak), is put to flight. Whence: "Grieve not the Holy Spirit of God, whereby you are sealed" etc. Sinning, therefore, we grieve the Holy Ghost. Doing well, we prepare him rest. What, therefore, he says of the seventy elders, that the Spirit rested in them, set forth the praise of their life and their virtues.
06_interl240: he sets forth the praise of their life
06_marg240: And the Spirit rested in them, or upon them, and they prophesied, etc. The Spirit works continually and suffers no idleness where worthy matter for working is supplied. In all, therefore, who prophesied the Spirit rested, but not as in the Saviour, for which reason it is said of him: There shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise up out of his root, and the Spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and of understanding, etc. For see that upon no other is the Spirit of the Lord described to have rested with this sevenfold virtue; by which the substance of the divine Spirit (since it could not be by one name) is explained by divers words, and is prophesied to rest upon him. Hence John also says: He who sent me to baptize with water said to me: He upon whom thou shalt see the Spirit of God descending, and remaining upon him, he it is. For he added "and remaining upon him", that this might be a sign in the Saviour which could not be shown in another. For of him alone was it said: Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth. For because he alone is the one who did no sin, therefore in him alone the Spirit remained and abode. It is clear therefore that all the rest were under sin, nor is it fitting that we should say the Spirit remained in them in the time of sin. For Moses himself, when he had already received the Spirit, bears witness that he sinned, when he said: Hear, ye unbelievers. Can we bring forth water for you out of this rock? For in these words he did not sanctify God, that is, he did not trust in the power of God. When therefore he spoke these things, he spoke not by the Holy Ghost but by the spirit of sin. It is certain therefore that the other prophets at times had the Spirit of God, at times had not. Hence David also says: "And take not thy spirit from me", in which he shows that it can be taken away. But in what follows he asks for it again as taken away: "Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation, and strengthen me with a perfect spirit." No one says, either, that Solomon judged judgments, or built the temple to the Lord, otherwise than in the Holy Ghost; or again that in the Holy Ghost he made temples to demons, or bent his side to impious women. The prophet Abdo too was sent by the Lord to Bethel, and spoke the words of the Lord in the Spirit of God; yet not in the same Spirit did he transgress the command of the Lord, by which he was forbidden to eat bread in Bethel; and therefore he was slain by a lion. But I (though I do not pronounce it in every case) think there are also certain common doings of men which, though they are not without sin, yet do not seem worthy that the Holy Ghost should be present in them; as lawful marriages are indeed without sin, yet when conjugal acts are done the Holy Ghost is not given, even if a prophet performs them. For there are many other things in which human strength alone suffices, and the matter neither needs nor befits the presence of the Holy Ghost.
06_marg241: Not by neglect of the Lord's command, but by the devotion of humility, judging themselves unworthy of receiving so great a gift; therefore God, the judge of hearts, judged them worthy and showed them so.
06_interl241: He willed all to prophesy who did not grudge the good he had.
06_marg242: WHY, HE SAITH, HAST THOU EMULATION FOR ME, etc. GREGORY. The loving mind of pastors, because it seeks not its own glory but the Author's, wishes to be helped by all in what it does. For the faithful preacher wishes, if it could be, that the truth which he alone is not sufficient to speak should sound from the mouths of all. Whence when Josue wished to withstand the two who remained in the camp and prophesied, it is said to him by Moses: Why hast thou emulation for me? O that all the people might prophesy, and that he would give them his spirit! For he willed all to prophesy who did not grudge others the good he had.
06_marg243: RABANUS. The carnal people of the Jews, having taken the heavenly food, desired flesh; but God so tempered the judgment as to punish the wicked, and not to deny nourishment to the frail, and in the very grant to hint at something spiritual. For he gave them to eat not of wild beasts, not of four-footed or earthly animals, but of birds, that they might learn to desire heavenly things rather than earthly, spiritual rather than bodily. For the nature of birds came forth from the waters, but acquires for itself a dwelling in the air. Those therefore who eat birds are warned to lift the heart from the lowest things to the highest, that though they live in earthly bodies, they may always seek heavenly things in mind, according to that of the Apostle: Walking in the flesh, we do not war according to the flesh. "But our conversation is in heaven."
06_marg244: ISIDORE. The thirteenth station is at the graves of lust, where the people, loathing the heavenly bread, desired the flesh of Egypt, and a sudden fire devoured many. By which we are taught, we who leave the conversation of the world and the Egyptian fleshpots, that is, the heats of carnal desires, not to murmur against the heavenly bread, nor seek the poisons of the Egyptians, who are of great flesh, but the simple food of manna; that is, that we lead a pure and heavenly life. For if, after receiving the angelic manna, which is the heavenly life or doctrine, we again seek the flesh of Egypt, that is, the carnal pleasures of the world, and the nausea of former lust, we shall at once be tormented by the fire of the Lord, and our desire will be turned into tombs, so that we are whited sepulchres, which outwardly appear beautiful, but within are full of dead men's bones and of all filthiness.
06_marg245: THEY CAME UNTO HASEROTH, etc. JEROME. The fourteenth station is in the wilderness of Pharan, which is turned "courts". In this Aaron and Mary murmur against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman. And mark this, prudent reader, that after virtue was completed in the number twelve (because Israel grew proud and at the graves of lust desired the flesh of Egypt), it lays the foundation again and enters the courts, that is, the forecourts, of virtue; showing us that those who stand can fall, and those who have fallen can rise again. For Jesus is set for the fall and for the resurrection of many. Who says by the Prophet: Shall not he that falleth rise again?
06_marg246: The fourteenth station is in the wilderness of Haseroth. In this Aaron and Mary offended by detracting from their brother because he had taken a foreign wife; and at once Mary, struck with leprosy, broke out white; because the priestly people, disparaging the Church gathered from the Gentiles before Christ the Saviour, is covered with the leprosy of sin. Nor does it return to the tabernacle of God until the fulness of the Gentiles has come in. For then it will receive its former health, when the knowledge of the sevenfold Spirit has brought it back to pardon.
